question.text: Under Section 14 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, the scope of protection extended to a reporting entity and its officers in certain cases is best described as protection from:

answer.text: Only criminal proceedings arising from such cases
Only civil proceedings arising from such cases
Both civil and criminal proceedings against the reporting entity, its directors, and employees in certain cases
Disciplinary proceedings by the regulator but not court proceedings

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the scope of Section 14 as no civil or criminal proceedings against reporting entities, their directors, and their employees in certain cases. So the protection covers both civil and criminal proceedings rather than only one of them. The Trap: The first two options each mention only one type of proceeding (criminal or civil), but the scope label in the workbook covers both. The fourth option incorrectly narrows the protection to regulatory disciplinary actions. Note: Page 28 of the NISM Series XXIV workbook supports the Section 14 scope label "no civil or criminal proceedings against reporting entities, directors, and employees in certain cases." Fuller wording (good-faith furnishing, safe-harbour rationale, link to STR filing) was not located in the pages checked.
